option_C: A rigid c-spine collar should be applied.
option_D: A rigid c-spine collar should be applied and the patient should be maintained on a hard spinal board
gpt5_rationale: In an unconscious trauma patient with unclear mechanism, cervical spine injury must be assumed and a rigid cervical collar should be applied. Routine prolonged immobilization on a hard spinal board is not recommended because of pressure injury risk and is mainly for extrication/transfer.

stem: A neonate has excessive salivation and respiratory distress. Attempts to pass a nasogastric catheter fails because it coils at the back of the throat. A chest film shows a gasless abdomen and right upper lobe atelectasis. The most likely diagnosis is?
option_A: Esophageal atresia with distal tracheoesophageal fistula
option_D: Esophageal atresia with proximal and distal fistula
gpt5_rationale: Failure to pass an NG tube indicates esophageal atresia, and a gasless abdomen means there is no distal fistula supplying air to the stomach. Right upper lobe atelectasis suggests aspiration through a proximal tracheoesophageal fistula, fitting esophageal atresia with proximal and distal fistula among the given choices.

stem: GFR may be assessed by the various methods except:
gpt5_rationale: GFR is assessed directly or estimated using eGFR equations, inulin clearance, and cystatin C. Serum creatinine alone is not a GFR measurement method; it is only a marker used to estimate renal function.

stem: A 40-year old presented to the gynaecologist with complaints of profuse vaginal discharge. There was no discharge from the cervix on speculum examination. The diagnosis of bacteria vaginosis was made based on the following on microscopy except:
gpt5_rationale: Bacterial vaginosis on microscopy is characterized by clue cells, reduced/absent lactobacilli, and abundant gram-variable coccobacilli (typically Gardnerella-associated flora). Presence of Bacteroides is not a standard direct microscopic diagnostic criterion.

stem: A 55-year-old woman who is being managed for DVT with warfarin started bleeding from GIT. Further assessment revealed that she had deranged liver and renal function. To prevent pulmonary embolism which of the following should be done urgently
option_B: b.	Stop the warfarin therapy and watchfully wait
option_C: c.	To insert an IVC filter
option_D: d.	To treat the liver for 6 weeks before restarting the warfarin
gpt5_rationale: She has acute DVT but now has active GI bleeding and organ dysfunction, making anticoagulation unsafe. In this setting, urgent placement of an IVC filter is indicated to reduce the risk of pulmonary embolism.

stem: A 45-year-old male patient complains of dysphagia of 2 years’ duration. He seems to have greater difficulty swallowing liquids than solids. Recently he has noticed that at night he is woken up by coughing. He has lost about 7–8 kg in weight in 6 months. The most likely diagnosis in this patient is
gpt5_rationale: Dysphagia that is worse for liquids than solids suggests a motility disorder rather than a mechanical obstruction. Nocturnal coughing from regurgitation and long-standing symptoms are classic for achalasia.

stem: A 45-year-old woman with long-standing, well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis develops severe pain and swelling in the left elbow over 2 days. She is not sexually active. You suspect septic arthritis. If you are correct, which of the following is the most likely organism to cause septic arthritis in this case?
gpt5_rationale: In adults with rheumatoid arthritis, septic arthritis is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Gonococcal arthritis is less likely here given her age and lack of sexual activity.

stem: Mr. Adu has been feeling sad and has lost interest in pleasurable for the past 3 months. He has heard that people with depression may be prescribed an SSRI, and wants to know what SSRI stands for. You tell Mr Adu that SSRI stands for
gpt5_rationale: SSRI stands for Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor. None of the listed options match that expansion exactly.

stem: A two year old male child presents at the emergency room with a five-day history of cough and breathlessness. Examination reveals cardiomegaly, central cyanosis but no cardiac murmurs. The most likely diagnosis is:
gpt5_rationale: Central cyanosis with cardiomegaly in a young child and absence of a murmur strongly suggests a cyanotic congenital heart disease rather than pneumonia or an acyanotic ASD. Tricuspid atresia can present with cyanosis and may have minimal or no audible murmur.

stem: 7)	A 6-week-old child arrives with a complaint of “breathing fast” and a cough. On examination you note the child to have no temperature elevation, a respiratory rate of 65 breaths per minute, and her oxygen saturation to be 94%. Physical examination also is significant for rales and rhonchi. The past medical history for the child is positive for an eye discharge at 3 weeks of age, which was treated with a topical antibiotic drug. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this child’s condition?
gpt5_rationale: This infant’s afebrile pneumonia with tachypnea at 6 weeks plus prior neonatal conjunctivitis is classic for Chlamydia trachomatis. That organism is not listed among the options, so none of the provided answers is correct.

stem: A 24-year-old man presents to the ER with an acute abdomen. He has a generally tender abdomen with guarding and rebound tenderness. The bowel sounds are absent. He is being managed for generalised peritonitis secondary to a hollow viscus perforation. The imaging investigation appropriate to demonstrate air in the abdomen is
gpt5_rationale: An erect chest X-ray is the standard plain film to detect free subdiaphragmatic air from a perforated hollow viscus. It is more sensitive than an abdominal X-ray for pneumoperitoneum.

stem: A previously healthy 18-month-old has been in a separate room from his family. The family notices the sudden onset of coughing, which resolves in a few minutes. Subsequently, the patient appears to be normal except for increased amounts of drooling and refusal to take foods orally. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this toddler’s condition
gpt5_rationale: A brief, sudden coughing episode while unsupervised followed by persistent drooling and refusal to eat strongly suggests aspiration or ingestion of a foreign body. Epiglottitis and croup typically cause ongoing respiratory symptoms and systemic illness rather than a transient coughing event with subsequent dysphagia.

stem: A 5-year-old child presents with recurrent afebrile generalized seizures. Examination reveals head circumference of 46 cm. Other findings are apparently normal. Which of the following is not useful in the evaluation of the child’s condition?
gpt5_rationale: The child likely has microcephaly with epilepsy, where etiologic evaluation focuses on prenatal/perinatal insults and developmental history. IQ testing showing 65 reflects associated impairment but is less useful for identifying the cause of the condition compared with asphyxia, severe jaundice, or delayed speech.

stem:
4 hours after eating salad at a restaurant, a 25-year-old lady presents to the ER with nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps. She later started to experience non-bloody, non-mucoid watery diarrhea. 
The most likely organism is?
gpt5_rationale: Rapid onset of nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, and watery diarrhea within 4 hours after eating salad is classic for preformed enterotoxin food poisoning due to Staphylococcus aureus. The other options usually have a longer incubation period and different typical clinical patterns.

stem: A 30-year-old female consults you that her mother has been diagnosed with breast and ovarian cancer. Similarly, her maternal aunt was treated for breast cancer two years prior. She would like to be screened for breast cancer. Which screening approach IS NOT appropriate for her?
gpt5_rationale: With a strong family history suggestive of hereditary breast-ovarian cancer syndrome, appropriate screening includes clinical breast examination, mammography, and often MRI for high-risk women. Ultrasound is not a standard primary screening modality in this setting and is usually adjunctive or diagnostic.

stem: A 28-year-old 62 para 1 at 28 weeks' gestation attends the antenatal clinic to discuss vaginal birth after caesarean section (VBAC). She had a previous emergency caesarean section 3 years ago for undiagnosed breech in labour. Which one of the following is true concerning VBAC?
option_A: Intermittent monitoring during labour is recommended.
option_C: It is contraindicated in women with previous classical caesarean section.
option_D: The chances of successful vaginal birth is around 50%.
gpt5_rationale: VBAC is contraindicated after a previous classical caesarean because of the substantially increased risk of uterine rupture. The rupture risk after one prior lower-segment caesarean is usually around 0.5%, continuous rather than intermittent fetal monitoring is recommended, and success rates are typically about 70–75%.

stem:
A 62-year-old man who had prosthetic aortic valve replacement 6 weeks earlier presented with weight loss, night sweats and intermittent palpitations over the
past month. His heart rate is 88 bpm and regular. Blood pressure checked was 140/86 mmHg. He has a prosthetic valve murmur and splinter haemorrhages are found on examination of his fingernails. Echocardiogram done showed vegetations on the aortic valve. What is the most likely causative organism?
gpt5_rationale: This is early prosthetic valve endocarditis occurring within 2 months of valve replacement. Early PVE is classically caused by hospital-acquired organisms including Staphylococci and fungi; among the listed options, Candida albicans is the best match.

stem: A 38-year-old woman presents to the maternity day assessment unit with a history of swollen feet, headache and blurring of vision at 30 weeks' gestation. Her BP is 160/100, pulse rate 88 bpm, oxygen saturation (Sp O 2) 99% on air and normal temperature. Uterine height measures 26 cm. Qualitative analysis of urine reveals 3 plusses of protein. What would be the diagnosis in this clinical context?
gpt5_rationale: This presentation is most consistent with pre-eclampsia: new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks with significant proteinuria plus headache and visual symptoms, and possible fetal growth restriction. Since pre-eclampsia is not among the options, none of the listed choices is correct.

stem: A 47 years old man presents with a 2 day history of disorientation, auditory and visual hallucinaitons. His wife says he has been complaining of headaches 2 days prior to presentation. His blood pressure is 212/125 mmHg. This is his first such episode. He most likely has;
gpt5_rationale: Acute onset psychosis with disorientation, recent headache, and severe hypertension strongly suggests a medical/organic etiology rather than a primary psychiatric disorder. The first episode at age 47 also makes primary psychotic illness less likely.

stem: A 34-year-old woman presents with galactorrhoea, loss of libido and amenorrhoea for 4 months. MRI of the brain showed a macroadenoma with pressure on the optic chiasm. Which visual defect is likely to be found on examination?
gpt5_rationale: A pituitary macroadenoma compressing the optic chiasm classically affects the crossing nasal retinal fibers, causing loss of temporal visual fields in both eyes. This produces bitemporal hemianopia.

stem: A 57-year old nulliparous woman comes 2 weeks after noticing a lump in the right breast. Her last mammogram was done 4 years ago and showed no abnormalities. Menopause began 2 years ago, during which time the patient was prescribed hormone replacement therapy for severe hot flashes and vaginal dryness. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the right breast shows a firm, non-tender mass close to the nipple. There are no changes in the skin or nipple and there is no palpable axillary adenopathy. The abdomen is soft and nontender. Mammography shows a suspicious 2 cm mass adjacent to the nipple. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
gpt5_rationale: A suspicious palpable breast mass on mammography requires tissue diagnosis, and fine needle aspiration is an appropriate next step for initial pathologic evaluation. Serum tumor markers and bone scan are not indicated before diagnosis, and excisional biopsy is not first-line when less invasive sampling is available.

stem: A 50-year-old farmer presents with diarrhoea, flatulence, joint pains and gradual weight loss over the past 6 months. A small bowel biopsy shows villous atrophy and periodic acid-Schiff positive macrophages. What is the most likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: The biopsy finding of villous atrophy with PAS-positive macrophages is classic for Whipple disease. Since Whipple disease is not among the listed options, none of the choices is correct.

stem: A patient presents with small bowel obstruction and a history of appendectomy 10 years ago. She is given fluid, an NGT tube, and a Foley catheter. What are the clinical signs or symptoms that indicate the need for surgery?
gpt5_rationale: In small bowel obstruction, peritonitis suggests bowel ischemia, strangulation, or perforation and is a clear indication for urgent surgery. Vomiting, constipation, and abdominal distension are common features of obstruction but are not by themselves definitive indications for operative intervention.

stem: A 30-year-old female presents with a chief complaint of palpitations. A 24-h Holter monitor is obtained and shows occasional unifocal PVCs and premature atrial contractions. Which of the following is the best antiarrhythmic management in this patient?
gpt5_rationale: Occasional unifocal PVCs and PACs in an otherwise likely healthy young patient are usually benign but can be symptomatically improved with beta blockers. Quinidine and digoxin are not appropriate first-line therapy, and anxiolytics do not directly treat the ectopy.

stem: A 20-year-old primigravida, unbooked, was rushed into the emergency room unconscious following repeated episodes of convulsions. Blood pressure checked on admission was 150/100 mmHg. Urinalysis revealed 3+ of proteinuria. She was thereafter given intravenous injection of Magnesium sulphate. The following is untrue regarding Magnesium sulphate:
option_A: Is given to cases of imminent eclampsia
option_B: The aim is to reduce blood pressure
option_C: Acts on the central nervous system causing depression
gpt5_rationale: Magnesium sulphate is used in eclampsia/imminent eclampsia for seizure prevention and control, not primarily to lower blood pressure. It acts as a CNS depressant and is excreted by the kidneys.

stem: You assess a 26-year-old woman with a diagnosis of bipolar disorder in the emergency department. She is speaking very quickly and is difficult to interrupt. She scarcely finishes a sentence before starting another. She speaks about a range of topics but her words make sense and the topics are clearly linked to one another. What sign is she exhibiting?
gpt5_rationale: Rapid, excessive, hard-to-interrupt speech with understandable content and linked ideas is characteristic of pressure of speech, commonly seen in mania. The other options involve language impairment, drifting off-topic, or poverty of speech.

stem: Consent is being obtain from a 24-year-old for a diagnostic laparoscopy and it is correctly documented that there is risk of laparotomy if any injury to bowel, bladder or blood vessels were to occur during the procedure. The patient wishes to know what proportion of cases would be converted to a laparotomy my should an injury occur?
gpt5_rationale: When bowel, bladder, or vascular injury occurs during diagnostic laparoscopy, a substantial proportion require open conversion for repair. Among the options, 67% is the best-supported estimate commonly cited for consent discussions.

stem: A 36 year old factory worker developed itchy, annular scaly plaques in both groins Application of a corticosteroid ointment led to temporary relief but the plaques continued to extend at the periphery. The most likely diagnosis is?
gpt5_rationale: Itchy annular scaly plaques in the groin with peripheral extension are classic for tinea cruris. Temporary improvement with topical corticosteroid can occur, but steroids often mask and worsen dermatophyte infection.

stem:
Hypercortisolism promotes deposition of adipose tissue in upper face (moon facies), interscapular area (buffalo hump), supraclavicular fat pads & mesenteric bed (truncal obesity). Rarely, episternal fatty tumors and mediastinal widening secondary to fat accumulation occur.
Most common cause of Cushing’s syndrome is?
gpt5_rationale: The most common overall cause of Cushing’s syndrome is exogenous glucocorticoid use. Endogenous adrenal causes like hyperplasia or neoplasia are much less common.

stem: A 65-year-old male develops the onset of severe knee pain over 24 hours. The knee is red, swollen, and tender. He has a history of diabetes mellitus and cardiomyopathy. An x-ray of the knee shows linear calcification. Definitive diagnosis is best made by which of the following?
option_B: Arthrocentesis and identification of positively birefringent rhomboid crystals
gpt5_rationale: Acute red, swollen knee with chondrocalcinosis (linear calcification) on x-ray is classic for calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease. Definitive diagnosis is by arthrocentesis showing positively birefringent rhomboid crystals.

stem: You are asked to consult on a 14-year-old boy who was hospitalized overnight with a fever of 39 C. He is toxic appearing and has been sick for six days. He had a bad upper respiratory infection two weeks ago, but over the last few days has had increasing headaches, pain in his right eye, and increasing nasal discharge. Two days ago, he was noted to have swelling and redness around his right eye, but this spread to his left one day ago. He now has proptosis and chemosis in the right eye with some limitation of eye motion and redness, as well as swelling and chemosis of the left eye. Which diagnosis is most concerning for this patient?
gpt5_rationale: Progression from sinus infection to severe headache, toxic appearance, proptosis, chemosis, ophthalmoplegia, and spread from one eye to bilateral orbital findings is classic for cavernous sinus thrombosis. Bilateral eye involvement is especially concerning because the cavernous sinuses communicate across the midline.

stem: 43. A 32-year-old woman who after an emergency laparotomy started exhibiting signs of depression and confusion after being kept NPO for more than 7 days. Which of the electrolyte disturbances is responsible for these new developments
gpt5_rationale: After prolonged starvation/NPO status, refeeding or severe nutritional depletion can cause hypophosphataemia, which commonly presents with confusion, irritability, and neuropsychiatric symptoms. The other listed electrolyte abnormalities are less specifically linked to this postoperative starvation context.

stem: A 45 year old man is rushed to the emergency having been found lying in a pool of vomitus. His history is significant for chronic alcohol use. You notice he has multiple abrasions over his body. On your examination you find that extra-ocular movements are restricted on lateral gaze, and a horizontal nystagmus is present. He is disoriented and confused and has gait ataxia. What is the likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for Wernicke encephalopathy: confusion, ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus, and gait ataxia in a chronic alcohol user. Since Wernicke encephalopathy is not among the listed options, none of the choices is correct.

stem: 28)	A 16-year-old girl complains of dysuria of 1 week's duration. She was seen 4 days ago at an urgent care facility and was prescribed trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole because of abnormal urinalysis findings. Although she has taken the antibiotic as directed, she has had no relief from the dysuria. She has no nausea, vomiting, flank pain, vaginal discharge, or fever. Of the following, the MOST appropriate course of action is to
gpt5_rationale: Persistent dysuria despite appropriate empiric UTI therapy and absence of systemic symptoms should prompt reevaluation for non-UTI causes such as vulvovaginitis, herpes, or local irritation. A genital examination is the most appropriate next step before changing or adding treatment.

stem: A 56-year-old woman develops difficulty ambulating several weeks after receiving an influenza vaccine. She is found to have distal muscle weakness and areflexia in the lower extremities. During a 2-day observation period the weakness ascends, and she begins to notice weakness of the hands. She notices mild tingling, but the sensory examination is normal. The diagnosis of Guillain-Barré syndrome is strongly suspected. The workup of this patient is most likely to show which of the following?
option_C: Respiratory alkalosis by arterial blood gases
option_D: Abnormal EMG that shows axonal degeneration
gpt5_rationale: This presentation is classic for Guillain-Barré syndrome: ascending weakness, areflexia, and mild paresthesias after vaccination. Electrodiagnostic testing is typically abnormal in GBS, showing a peripheral neuropathy pattern; the other options fit myopathy, myasthenia gravis, or are not the most likely finding.

stem: A 21-year-old woman, who is known to have beta thalassemia major, attends the clinic for preconception counselling. What is the most relevant initial pre-pregnancy investigation to predict maternal complications of pregnancy?
gpt5_rationale: In beta thalassemia major, myocardial iron overload is a key predictor of maternal cardiac complications in pregnancy. Cardiac MRI (T2*) is the most relevant pre-pregnancy investigation because it best assesses cardiac iron loading and stratifies risk.

stem: A five-month old female infant whose parents are both bankers is brought into the emergency room with two-day history of passage of loose watery stool and two hours of irritability. She is exclusively fed on artificial milk. Physical examination reveals an infant weighing 7.5 kg with doughy skin and dry mucous membrane. The diagnosis is:
gpt5_rationale: An exclusively formula-fed infant with diarrhea, irritability, doughy skin, and dry mucous membranes is classic for hypernatremic dehydration. Doughy skin and neurologic irritability are key distinguishing features.

stem: The most appropriate treatment option for an eighty-year-old woman with a BMI of 25 presenting with post-menopausal bleeding and found to have Stage 1 a endometrial adenocarcinoma on MRI and hysteroscopy is:
gpt5_rationale: Stage IA endometrial adenocarcinoma is typically treated primarily with surgery: total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. In a fit 80-year-old with BMI 25 and no contraindication given, radiotherapy is not first-line and adjuvant radiotherapy is not routinely required for low-risk Stage IA disease.

stem: An elderly man has noticed three episodes of visual loss in his right eye. The vision in that eye goes black “like somebody pulling down a window shade.” The symptom lasts 20 to 30 min and resolves promptly. Between episodes he feels well. What is the likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: Transient monocular vision loss described as a 'window shade' is classic amaurosis fugax, usually due to retinal ischemia from ipsilateral internal carotid artery disease. The other vessels more typically cause binocular visual or focal cerebral deficits rather than isolated monocular blindness.

stem: A 75-year-old hypertensive woman presents with whirling vertigo, nausea, and weakness on the right side of her body. On exam she has nystagmus, left facial sensory loss, and right arm and leg weakness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: Vertigo, nausea, and nystagmus with crossed brainstem findings suggest a posterior circulation stroke involving the brainstem. The combination of left facial sensory loss and contralateral right-sided weakness is most consistent with a basilar territory lesion rather than carotid, MCA, or ACA disease.

stem: A 40-year-old male complains of exquisite pain and tenderness in the left ankle. There is no history of trauma. The patient is taking a mild diuretic for hypertension. On exam, the ankle is very swollen and tender. There are no other physical exam abnormalities. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
option_C: Begin allopurinol if uric acid level is elevated
option_D: Obtain ankle x-ray to rule out fracture
gpt5_rationale: An acutely swollen, exquisitely tender monoarticular joint requires arthrocentesis to distinguish gout from septic arthritis or other crystal arthropathies. Diuretic use supports gout risk, but infection must be excluded before empiric treatment or urate-lowering therapy.

stem: An 18-year-old man complains of a lack of sex drive and having no sense of smell. He is of normal height and weight. He has absence of facial, axillary and pubic hair. His penis and testes are small in size. What is the most likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: Hypogonadism with anosmia is classic for Kallmann syndrome due to GnRH deficiency. The absent secondary sexual characteristics and small testes/penis strongly support this diagnosis.

stem: Perimenopause refers to the time period preceding menopause, when fertility wanes and menstrual cycle irregularity increases. Onset of perimenopause precedes the final menses by 2-8 years, with mean duration of 4 years. Menopause is diagnosed retrospectively after how many months of amenorrhea?
gpt5_rationale: Natural menopause is diagnosed retrospectively after 12 months of amenorrhea. Since 12 months is not among the options provided, none of the listed choices is correct.

stem: A 33-year-old man presents with a painless penile ulcer which has persisted for 5 months. The lesion started as a papule which later ulcerated and has been enlarging. Physical examination reveals a nontender friable ulcer with rolled borders. Which of these is the most likely causative organism?
gpt5_rationale: A chronic, painless, friable genital ulcer with rolled borders is classic for granuloma inguinale (donovanosis). The causative organism is Klebsiella granulomatis, a Gram-negative rod.

stem: 35)	During a regular checkup of an 8-year-old child, you note a loud first heart sound with a fixed and widely split second heart sound at the upper left sternal border that does not change with respirations. The patient is otherwise active and healthy. Which of the following heart lesions most likely explains these findings?
gpt5_rationale: A fixed, widely split S2 that does not vary with respiration is classic for an atrial septal defect due to chronic right-sided volume overload and delayed pulmonic valve closure. The otherwise healthy, active child also fits a typical ASD presentation.

stem: A 28-year-old man is brought by ambulance to the emergency department after falling from the roof of his home four hours ago. Upon initial evaluation, he has visible deformities of his bilateral lower extremities and a positive FAST exam. Heart rate is 135, blood pressure 85/58, and urine output is 40 cc over 3 hours. According to ATLS guidelines, what percentage of his blood volume has this patient likely lost?
gpt5_rationale: He is tachycardic, hypotensive, and has markedly decreased urine output, which is consistent with ATLS Class IV hemorrhagic shock. Class IV shock corresponds to approximately 40-50% blood volume loss.

stem: A 75-year-old patient presents to the ER after a sudden syncopal episode. He is again alert and in retrospect describes occasional substernal chest pressure and shortness of breath on exertion. His lungs have a few bibasilar rales, and his blood pressure is 110/80. Which of the following classic findings should you expect to hear on cardiac auscultation?
option_A: A harsh systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur heard best at the upper right sternal border
option_B: A diastolic decrescendo murmur heard at the mid-left sternal border
option_C: A holosystolic murmur heard best at the apex
gpt5_rationale: Syncope, exertional chest pain, dyspnea, and bibasilar rales in an elderly patient are classic for symptomatic aortic stenosis. The expected murmur is a harsh systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur best heard at the upper right sternal border.

stem: A 9-year old boy presented with fever, vomiting, abdominal pain and passage of dark urine. He took a hypodermic injection for a foot injury in the preceding month. Physical examination revealed axillary temperature of 38.1⁰C, heart rate of 80/minute, moderate pallor and 6 cm tender hepatomegaly. The most likely diagnosis in the patient is:
gpt5_rationale: Fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, dark urine (suggesting hemoglobinuria), pallor, and tender hepatomegaly in a child are classic for severe falciparum malaria. The recent injection is less explanatory than the acute febrile hemolytic picture.

stem: A 20-year-old man is brought to the emergency room after rupturing his spleen in a motorcycle accident. His blood pressure on admission is 80/60 mmHg. Analysis of arterial blood gases demonstrates metabolic acidosis. This patient is most likely suffering from which of the following conditions?
gpt5_rationale: A ruptured spleen with severe hypotension indicates hemorrhagic shock causing poor tissue perfusion and lactic metabolic acidosis. Since hemorrhagic shock is not listed, neurogenic shock is the closest trauma-related shock option, though it is not the best physiologic match.

stem: An otherwise healthy 45-year-old schizophrenic comes to his psychiatrist for a routine visit. He has had a poor response to several trials of typical antipsychotics, as well as to risperidone and olanzapine. His psychiatrist recommends a trial of clozapine. Which of the following baseline tests should be ordered on this patient before starting this drug?
gpt5_rationale: Clozapine requires baseline and ongoing monitoring for serious adverse effects, especially agranulocytosis, but CBC/ANC is not listed. Among the available options, baseline liver function tests are the most appropriate because clozapine can also cause hepatotoxicity; thyroid tests, EEG, and BUN are not routine baseline requirements.

stem: A 19-year-old man is seen in the emergency department 20 minutes after a high-speed head-on collision with a tree, in which his car caught fire. He was not wearing a seat belt and was ejected from the vehicle. In the emergency department, he is alert, but he does not remember what happened. He admits to drinking a few beers earlier. Blood pressure is 75/40 mmHg and heart rate 140. His airway is patent. Breath sounds are equal bilaterally. Arterial blood gases reveal a Pa O 2 of 140, Sa O 2 of 98%, Pa CO 2 of 34, and p H of 7.33. He has burns to 15% TBSA, involving his anterior trunk and legs. His abdomen is covered with burns but appears distended; tenderness is hard to determine because of painful burn wounds. What is the most likely cause of his hypotension?
gpt5_rationale: This patient has severe blunt trauma with ejection, profound hypotension, tachycardia, and abdominal distension, which strongly suggests hemorrhagic shock from intra-abdominal bleeding. His burns involve only 15% TBSA, making burn shock unlikely this early, and his oxygenation does not support significant smoke inhalation injury.

stem:
A 17-year-old boy presents to the GP. Most recently he has suffered a respiratory tract infection and he is very distressed that on going to the bathroom he is urinating
frank blood. The only history of note is microscopic hematuria diagnosed in childhood.
Renal biopsy with histological staining is consistent with a diagnosis of Alport’s syndrome.
Which of the following other features is likely to be present?
gpt5_rationale: Alport syndrome is a hereditary nephritis due to type IV collagen defects and is associated with ocular abnormalities, classically anterior lenticonus and sometimes cataracts. Hearing loss occurs, but it is sensorineural rather than otosclerosis.

stem: Physical examination in pneumomediastinum reveals subcutaneous emphysema in suprasternal notch & Hamman’s sign, which is a crunching or clicking noise synchronous with heartbeat & best heard in what patient position?
gpt5_rationale: Hamman’s sign in pneumomediastinum is a precordial crunching/clicking sound synchronous with the heartbeat and is classically best heard when the patient is in the left lateral decubitus or supine position. Among the given options, supine is the best match.

stem:
A 22-year-old female presents with palpitations, anxiety, and heat intolerance. 
A small smooth goitre is palpated. She has fine tremors and sweaty palms. Her blood pressure is 126/72 mmHg, and pulse is 98 bpm and regular. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) level is < 0.01 m IU/L , and both her T 4 and T 3 are elevated. Thyroid scanning reveals a uniformly increased uptake of technetium. What diagnosis best fits with this clinical picture?
gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for Graves disease: diffuse toxic goiter with uniformly increased radionuclide uptake, suppressed TSH, and elevated T3/T4. None of the listed options matches this pattern; toxic adenoma and multinodular goiter produce focal/patchy uptake, while thyroiditis typically shows low uptake.

stem: A 39-year-old, para 0 woman attends for an elective caesarean section for breech presentation Her BMI is 25. She undergoes an uncomplicated procedure and is mobile on the ward the same day. What is the most appropriate step in venous thromboembolism prophylaxis
option_B: Early mobilisation, prevention of dehydration, therapeutic low molecular weight heparin for at least 10 days
option_C: Early mobilisation, prevention of dehydration, prophylactic dose low molecular weight heparin for at least 3 days
option_D: Prevention of dehydration and thromboembolic stockings
gpt5_rationale: After elective caesarean section, women without additional VTE risk factors generally require only early mobilisation and avoidance of dehydration. Age 39 alone does not usually mandate postnatal LMWH in this scenario.

stem: Almost two-thirds of filtered Na+ is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule. 25-30% occurs via apical Na+- K+- 2 Cl–co-transporter. 5% occurs in Distal convoluted tubule mediated by thiazide-sensitive Na+- Cl– co-transporter. Na+ reabsorption also occurs in cortical and medullary collecting ducts. Reabsorption of filtered sodium mediated by ‘Na+-K+-2 Cl cotransporter’ occurs in?
option_B: Thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle
gpt5_rationale: The apical Na+-K+-2Cl− cotransporter (NKCC2) is located in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, where about 25–30% of filtered sodium is reabsorbed. The distal convoluted tubule instead uses the thiazide-sensitive Na+-Cl− cotransporter.

stem: You need detailed information information about his most current episode and your consulting room can accommodate only one other person aside the patient. Which of the people who accompanied him will you prefer to join you?
gpt5_rationale: For detailed collateral history about the most recent episode in a limited private setting, a close family caregiver is usually preferred. The mother is more likely than the boss or police officer to know the patient’s recent symptoms and behavior in detail.

stem: A 28-year-old man comes to clinic because of an inguinal hernia. He works as a stonemason and first noticed the hernia when he developed a painful bulge while lifting a bag of cement. He has otherwise been healthy and takes no medications. An open inguinal hernia repair with mesh has been recommended. During a discussion of the anticipated risks, which of the following represents the most common complication?
gpt5_rationale: Chronic postoperative groin pain is the most common complication after open inguinal hernia repair, often due to nerve irritation or entrapment. Recurrence and reduced fertility are less common, and urinary retention is more typically a short-term postoperative issue rather than the most common overall complication.

stem: A 45-year-old woman is undergoing an abdominal hysterectomy for a history of heavy menstrual bleeding that has not responded to medical treatment. The patient has a past history of pelvic pain and the operation notes from a previous laparoscopy comment that the patient had 'pelvic adhesions' What is the most appropriate action in terms of protecting the ureter?
option_A: Mobilise the entire ureter with the aid of electrosurgery to reduce the blood loss
option_C: Perform a preoperative MRI and Intravenous urogram to assess the ureters
gpt5_rationale: Prior pelvic adhesions increase the risk of ureteric injury during abdominal hysterectomy. Preoperative ureteric stenting can help identify and protect the ureters in difficult pelvic dissection, whereas routine MRI/IVU is not the key protective step and extensive ureteric mobilisation may itself increase injury risk.

stem: An 8-month old infant presents with the history of excessive crying and associated passage of bloody mucoid stool. These symptoms were preceded by an upper respiratory tract infection. On examination he is pale, irritable with palpable sausage shaped mass in the abdomen. The most likely diagnosis is:
gpt5_rationale: An 8-month-old with intermittent crying, bloody mucoid 'red currant jelly' stool, pallor/irritability, and a palpable sausage-shaped abdominal mass is classic for intussusception. A preceding viral URI is a common trigger due to lymphoid hyperplasia.

stem: A 55-year-old diabetic lady presents with right upper quadrant pain for the past 2 days. She has had shorter episodes of similar pain on and off over the preceding 2 years. On examination she is febrile, has jaundice and right upper quadrant tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?

stem: . A 23-year-old woman with history of previously well controlled Type 1 diabetes reports with having multiple recent episodes of hypoglycaemia. Her blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg with a postural drop of 10 mmHg. Initial investigations done were significant for a normocytic anaemia with haemoglobin of 10 g/dL and sodium of 130 mmol/L . stem: A 46-year-old man is diagnosed with an estrogen receptor-positive invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast after having discovered a lump 3 months before. stem: A 65-year-old man presents with a 3-cm hard mass in the right upper cervical region (Level II). If this is a metastatic lymph node, which of the following is the most likely primary site for the malignancy
gpt5_rationale: Level II upper cervical nodes most commonly receive lymphatic drainage from the oral cavity and oropharyngeal region. Among the listed options, the oral cavity is the most likely primary source of a metastatic node in this location.

stem: A patient has a ventouse delivery. Two days later she reports general malaise, fever and feeling unwell. With sepsis, which is the first clinical sign to deteriorate, which can be detected through the use of early warning scores?
gpt5_rationale: In sepsis, an increased respiratory rate is often the earliest physiological sign of deterioration and is a key trigger in early warning scores. Hypotension, hypoxia, and altered consciousness typically occur later.

Which medication should be used to 'prime' the cervix prior to the hysteroscopy?
gpt5_rationale: Misoprostol is commonly used for cervical priming before hysteroscopy, especially in postmenopausal patients where cervical dilation may be more difficult. Mifepristone is not standard for this indication, and NSAIDs do not prime the cervix.

stem: A 68-year-old woman is admitted at the medical ward for acute kidney injury. Results of her kidney function test come in showing a potassium level of 7.0 mmol/L . What is the appropriate medication to give next in her management?
gpt5_rationale: A potassium of 7.0 mmol/L is severe hyperkalemia and the immediate priority is cardiac membrane stabilization with IV calcium gluconate. Insulin/dextrose and salbutamol help shift potassium intracellularly, while calcium resonium removes potassium more slowly.

stem: A 4-hour old baby delivered at 29 weeks of gestation has a loud grunt, respiratory rate of 96/minute, SPO 2 of 57%, flaring of alae nasi and mild chest wall retraction at the sixth hours of life. The most likely diagnosis is:
gpt5_rationale: A 29-week premature infant developing severe respiratory distress within the first hours of life is most typical of surfactant-deficient respiratory distress syndrome. TTN is more common in term/near-term infants, congenital diaphragmatic hernia usually has characteristic asymmetric chest/scaphoid abdomen findings, and congenital pneumonia is less classically immediate in this context.

stem: A 33-year-old man complains of episodes of severe unilateral headache. The pain is localized to one cheekbone and is described as “like an icepick.” Each headache lasts 30 to 60 min but may recur several times a day; walking around helps the pain somewhat. He notices lacrimation of the eye on the affected side, usually associated with clear rhinorrhea. What is the likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for cluster headache: severe unilateral orbital/cheek pain lasting 30–60 minutes, recurring multiple times daily with ipsilateral lacrimation and rhinorrhea, and restlessness. Since cluster headache is not among the listed options, none of the choices is correct.

stem: A 39-year-old male presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain and vomiting. He prefers to sit bending forward. He has a tinge of jaundice and his abdomen is tender with an echymotic periumbilical region. What should be considered in this patient’s evaluation?

gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for acute pancreatitis, with pain relieved by leaning forward and Cullen's sign suggesting hemorrhagic pancreatitis. In evaluating pancreatitis, a recent endoscopic procedure such as ERCP is an important potential precipitating factor.

stem: 30. A 48-year-old man living in Liberia had an elective left hemicolectomy on account of adenocarcinoma of the caecum. Today is POD 2 following the surgery. stem: A 6 month old infant presented with multiple papules and exudative lesions on the face, scalp , trunk and few vesicles on the palms and soles for 2 weeks. His mother had history of itchy lesions. The most likely diagnosis is?
gpt5_rationale: The presentation strongly suggests infantile scabies, especially with papules, exudative lesions, vesicles on palms and soles, and an itchy mother. Since scabies is not among the listed options, none of the provided choices is correct.

An 82-year-old woman complains of worsening headaches and episodes of transient visual loss and diplopia. When she chews, her jaw muscles ache until she stops chewing. Exam reveals a tender nodular right temporal artery. She has a mild normocytic anemia; sedimentation rate is 95.
What is the likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: Elderly patient with new headache, jaw claudication, transient visual symptoms, tender nodular temporal artery, anemia, and markedly elevated ESR is classic for giant cell (temporal) arteritis.

stem: An 18-year old girl is brought to the emergency department with worsening severe lower abdominal pain that started 6 hours ago. Her abdomen is tender particularly in the lower quadrants and there is guarding. She is tachycardic but her blood pressure is 135/78 mmHg. gpt5_rationale: In an 18-year-old with 6 hours of worsening severe lower abdominal pain, lower quadrant tenderness, guarding, and tachycardia, an acute surgical abdomen must be prioritized. Among the listed options, acute appendicitis is the most important diagnosis to urgently confirm or exclude.

stem: A 45-year-old man has sudden swelling of his right knee which is tender to touch. Joint aspiration reveals weakly positive birefringent crystals of calcium pyrophosphate. What is the most likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: Calcium pyrophosphate crystals indicate pseudogout (CPPD), which is classically associated with chondrocalcinosis and osteoarthritis-like joint disease. Among the given options, osteoarthritis is the closest match because pseudogout itself is not listed.

stem: Your hospital has recently had an increase in postoperative infections. As a result, you are formulating a new guideline that includes information on skin preparation and hair removal prior to surgery. What is the most appropriate method of hair removal prior to surgery?
gpt5_rationale: If hair must be removed before surgery, electric clippers are recommended because they reduce skin abrasions and lower surgical site infection risk compared with shaving. Shaving with razors increases microtrauma and infection risk.

stem: You observe a senior O&G Resident performing a caesarean section in the second stage of labour following an unsuccessful attempt at operative vaginal delivery. There is some difficulty with delivery of the baby. What next step is likely to be performed?
option_A: Use a forceps blade to disimpact head by 'scooping the head

gpt5_rationale: In a second-stage caesarean with an impacted fetal head after failed operative vaginal delivery, the usual next step is vaginal disimpaction by an assistant elevating the head with direct upward pressure. Forceps blade use is not standard, repeated abdominal attempts alone are less effective and risk trauma, and waiting for the consultant delays urgent delivery.

stem: A newly admitted patient has burns on both lower limbs. The burned areas appear white and leather like. No blisters or bleeding are present. The patient states that she feels very little pain. This injury can likely be categorized as
gpt5_rationale: White, leathery skin with absent blisters/bleeding and minimal pain is classic for a full-thickness burn, which destroys dermal nerve endings. Superficial and partial-thickness burns are usually more painful and often blister.

stem: 24 yr old old immunocompromised patient had a procedure and stayed for about 2 weeks on admission in the hospital and was placed on broad spectrum antibiotics for some time. He later developed clostridium deficile infection. Which of the following is the least risk factor?
gpt5_rationale: Major risk factors for C. difficile include recent broad-spectrum antibiotic use, prolonged hospitalization, and immunocompromised status. Advanced age is a risk factor, but this patient is 24 years old, so age is the least relevant risk factor here.

stem: You are performing a splenectomy on a patient with hypersplenism. Thrombocytopenia is the major problem with this patient. Special attention to which technical aspect of the procedure is advised?
option_A: Ligation of the splenic artery before the vein
option_B: Division of the short gastric vessels before approach to the hilum
option_C: Medial visceral rotation of the entire spleen, pancreas and leftcolon.
option_D: Minimal touching or manipulation of the spleen
gpt5_rationale: In hypersplenism with severe thrombocytopenia, the enlarged spleen is fragile and manipulation can worsen platelet sequestration or provoke bleeding. Therefore, the spleen should be handled as little as possible during splenectomy.

stem: A 60-year-old white female presents with epigastric pain, nausea and vomiting, heart rate of 50, and pronounced first-degree AV block on ER cardiac monitor. Blood pressure is 130/80. Which of the following coronary arteries is most likely to be involved in this process?
gpt5_rationale: Inferior wall MI commonly presents with nausea/vomiting, sinus bradycardia, and AV nodal delay due to ischemia of the AV node. The AV node is most often supplied by the right coronary artery, but since it is not listed, the circumflex is the best available choice because it can supply the AV node in left-dominant circulation.

stem: A 23-year-old presented with a lower abdominal pain of 1-week duration and 6 weeks history of Amenorrhoea. Ultrasound scan reveals pregnancy in the uterus and another in the interstitial of the tube. The appropriate diagnosis
gpt5_rationale: Simultaneous intrauterine pregnancy and an ectopic pregnancy in the interstitial part of the tube is a heterotopic pregnancy. Option A appears to mean this despite the wording 'heterogenous.'

stem: A 37-year-old man is brought to the doctor by his family because of a rapid intellectual decline over the past 2 months. Exam reveals slow writhing movements with dystonic posturing. His father died of a similar illness. What is the likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: Rapid cognitive decline with slow writhing movements and dystonic posturing suggests a neurodegenerative/metabolic disorder rather than an isolated movement symptom. Among the options, Wilson’s disease best fits this presentation in a relatively young adult.

stem: A 25-year old woman, injured in a motor vehicular crash is admitted to the emergency department Hi pupils react sluggishly and his eyes open to painful stimuli. He does not follow commands but she moans periodically. His right arm is deformed and does not respond to painful stimulus; however, his left hand reaches purposefully toward the painful stimulus. gpt5_rationale: GCS = Eye 2 (opens to pain) + Verbal 2 (moans/incomprehensible sounds) + Motor 5 (localizes pain with the left hand; best motor response counts despite the injured right arm) = 9.

stem: A 23-year-old man is brought to casualty following a motorcycle collision. His airway and breathing was noted to be intact, but he is bleeding heavily from his left lower extremity, which has suffered a traumatic amputation. While attempting to obtain intravenous access, he is noted to be hypotensive. Which of the following is true?

stem: A 3-day old neonate delivered at term presents with oozing of blood from the umbilical cord stump and passage of dark stools of six hours duration. He had stopped sucking and became breathless just before presentation. Which of the following statements is valid?

stem: A twenty five-year-old girl presents with mid-cycle pain on a regular monthly basis. She is sexually active and does not take any contraception. The pain quickly resolves after 24 hours. She has a regular 28-day cycle. The likely cause of the pain is:
gpt5_rationale: Brief, recurrent mid-cycle pain in a woman with a regular 28-day cycle that resolves within 24 hours is classic for ovulation pain, i.e., mittelschmerz. The other options typically cause more persistent or differently timed pelvic pain.

stem: A 17-year-old woman, who is obese, reports to the hospital with a three-month history of amenorrhoea. She is noticed to have facial hair. Her blood pressure is 126/80 mmHg and body mass index is 32 kg/m2. What is the next most appropriate investigation?
gpt5_rationale: Obesity, amenorrhoea, and hirsutism in a 17-year-old strongly suggest hyperandrogenism, most commonly PCOS. The next investigation is serum testosterone to assess androgen excess and help distinguish PCOS from androgen-secreting causes.

stem: A healthy 54-year-old lady is due to attend the outpatient postmenopausal bleeding hysteroscopy clinic. Which medication should she be advised to consider taking prior to her attendance at the clinic?
gpt5_rationale: For outpatient hysteroscopy, simple oral analgesia such as paracetamol is commonly advised beforehand to reduce procedural discomfort. Routine use of benzodiazepines, opioids, or prostaglandins is not generally recommended for a healthy postmenopausal woman attending clinic hysteroscopy.

stem: A patient who has been on antiretrovirals for 6 years and who has maintained undetectable viral loads with his first-line regimen presents with an HIV-RNA viral load of 245 copies/ml. Which of the following is TRUE?

stem: A 52-year-old man who is known to have alcoholic cirrhosis is admitted at the Emergency Department with worsening ascites and abdominal pain. stem: An 18-year-old male who is admitted to the hospital because of psychotic behavior is found to have a proximal “wing-beating” tremor, dystonia, and incoordination. Serum transaminases are moderately elevated, brownish corneal deposits are noted on slit-lamp exam. What is the likely diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for Wilson disease: psychosis, wing-beating tremor, dystonia, incoordination, elevated transaminases, and Kayser-Fleischer rings. Wilson disease is not among the listed options.

stem: A 58-year-old man has been found to persistent have systolic blood pressure readings between 145 and 155 mmHg and diastolic pressures between 80 and 95 mmHg when checked at routine visits at the hospital. gpt5_rationale: Repeated elevated clinic readings with a normal reading today raise the possibility of white-coat hypertension. The next step is to confirm the diagnosis with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring before starting treatment.

stem: A 20-year-old male complains of arthritis and eye irritation. He has a history of burning on urination. On exam, there is a joint effusion of the right knee and a dermatitis of the glans penis. Which of the following is correct?

stem: A 43-year-old lady with a history of heavy menstrual bleeding and a scan suggesting a polyp is due to undergo an outpatient hysteroscopy. Which distension medium is routinely recommended due to its improved quality of image and speed of the procedure?
gpt5_rationale: For outpatient hysteroscopy, normal saline is generally preferred over carbon dioxide because it gives better visualization and often allows faster completion. Among the listed options, Purosol is the fluid distension medium corresponding to this routine recommendation.

stem: A 19-year-old man is seen after collapsing during an argument with his roommate. He has been experiencing palpitations and once fainted while playing basketball. He is otherwise fit and well. gpt5_rationale: Syncope with palpitations triggered by emotion/exercise plus a prolonged QTc strongly suggests congenital long QT syndrome. None of the listed options characteristically causes a prolonged corrected QT interval.

stem: A 50-year-old man known to have esophageal varices presents after a bout of massive haematemesis that day. He is pale, with a blood pressure of 80/52 mmHg and a pulse rate of 120/min. Which one of these statements is NOT TRUE?

gpt5_rationale: In acute variceal haemorrhage, vasoactive therapy such as terlipressin and prophylactic antibiotics are indicated, and mortality is typically under 40% with modern management. Proton pump inhibitors are not specifically indicated for variceal bleeding unless a non-variceal upper GI source is suspected or confirmed.

stem: A 60-year-old female complains of dry mouth and a gritty sensation in her eyes. She states it is sometimes difficult to speak for more than a few minutes. There is no history of diabetes mellitus or neurologic disease. The patient is on no medications. On exam, the buccal mucosa appears dry and the salivary glands are enlarged bilaterally. gpt5_rationale: Dry eyes, dry mouth, difficulty speaking, and bilateral salivary gland enlargement strongly suggest Sjögren syndrome. The best next step is objective evaluation with Schirmer testing and serologic autoantibodies (eg, anti-SSA/SSB); lip biopsy is typically reserved when diagnosis remains uncertain.

stem: A 79-year-old man has had abdominal pain for 4 days. An operation is performed, and a gangrenous appendix is removed. Why does acute appendicitis in elderly patients and in children have a worse prognosis?
option_B: The omentum and peritoneal cavity appear to be less efficient in localizing the disease in these age groups.
option_C: There may be a delay in establishing the right diagnosis in these age groups.
option_D: The appendix is in the pelvic position.
gpt5_rationale: In children and the elderly, the omentum and peritoneal defenses are less effective at walling off appendiceal inflammation, so perforation and generalized peritonitis occur more readily. This is the classic reason their prognosis is worse.

stem: A 36-year-old woman who is breastfeeding her first child complains of a smooth, mobile, painless lump in the outer quadrant of the right breast. Core biopsy is attempted and a white opaque fluid is expressed. The most likely diagnosis in this patient is:
gpt5_rationale: A painless, smooth, mobile breast lump in a breastfeeding woman with expression of white opaque fluid on biopsy is classic for a galactocele. Galactoceles are milk-retention cysts that occur during lactation.

stem: A 10-year-old boy presents with a history of sore throat three days ago. He now has a severe sore throat, only on the right side, with a fever of 38.5 C and trismus. On your exam, you can see soft palate swelling, most notably on the right, and the uvula is deviated to the left. There is edema and erythema of the uvula. Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?
gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for a peritonsillar abscess: unilateral severe sore throat, fever, trismus, soft palate swelling, and uvular deviation away from the affected side. That diagnosis is not listed among the options, so none of the provided choices is correct.

stem: A 27-year-old female presents with palpitations, weight loss, polyuria, diarrhea, and increased appetite for 3 weeks. Her past medical history is non-significant. Which of the following investigations is the most appropriate for this patient?
gpt5_rationale: Palpitations, weight loss, diarrhea, and increased appetite strongly suggest hyperthyroidism. Thyroid function tests are the most appropriate investigation to confirm this.

stem: A 40-year-old female complains of 7 weeks of pain and swelling in both wrists and knees. The patient complained of fatigue and lethargy several weeks before noticing the joint pain. The patient notes that after a period of rest, resistance to movement is more striking. On exam, the metacarpophalangeal joints and wrists are warm and tender. There are no other joint abnormalities. option_D: X-rays of the hand are likely to show joint space narrowing and erosion
gpt5_rationale: Symmetric inflammatory arthritis of the MCPs and wrists with morning stiffness and a fatigue prodrome is classic for early rheumatoid arthritis. Early plain films may still be normal, so obtaining serologies such as rheumatoid factor is appropriate.

stem: A 45-year-old male presents with a daily headache. He describes two attacks per day over the last 3 weeks. Each attack lasts about an hour and awakens the patient from sleep. gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for cluster headache: severe unilateral periorbital pain with autonomic symptoms, occurring in brief recurrent attacks that wake him from sleep. Cluster headache is not among the listed options.

stem: A 35-year-old nulliparous woman at 36 weeks' gestation was diagnosed with pre eclampsis She complains of headaches and visual disturbances. Her blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg and Hb 10 g/dl, platelets 90, ALT 88. She is at risk of the following complications except which one?
gpt5_rationale: She has severe pre-eclampsia features with neurologic symptoms, thrombocytopenia, and elevated ALT, which increase the risk of eclampsia, cerebral hemorrhage, and pulmonary edema. Placenta praevia is unrelated to pre-eclampsia and is not a typical complication.

stem: Hawa has a fear of spiders and sees a therapist for help. The therapist first teaches her deep relaxation breathing. Then she exposed Hawa to increasing grades of stimulus; a cartoon of a spider, a picture of a spider, a toy spider and then a real spider. gpt5_rationale: The therapist is pairing relaxation with a stepwise hierarchy of spider-related stimuli, moving from least to most anxiety-provoking. This is graded exposure (systematic desensitization-style exposure), not flooding or implosion.

A patient has 5 days of vomiting and generalized, colicky pain. Radiological examination is consistent with your diagnosis of small bowel obstruction. The blood work shows the following: WBC is 12.0, Cr 2.0 (normal <1.1), Na 130, K 2.5, Cl 90 BUN 18. What is your next step in management? 
 

 
.
option_A: Immediate surgery as she has confirmed bowel obstruction with an elevated WBC and renal failure and likely gangrenous bowel and continue resuscitation post-operatively.

option_C: Immediate resuscitation with normal saline or ringer’s lactate in 1.0L boluses until urine output established K replacement after urine output confirmed, check Hgb level and cross-match for possible transfusion and then consider surgery.

gpt5_rationale: This patient with SBO has significant volume depletion and pre-renal AKI plus hypokalemia, so the immediate priority is aggressive isotonic fluid resuscitation and NG/urine output monitoring before operative decision-making unless there are clear peritonitic/ischemic signs. Potassium should be replaced only after urine output is established because creatinine is elevated, and transfusion is not indicated unless hemoglobin or clinical status warrants it.

stem: A 32-year-old male with no medical conditions presents with generalized muscle aches and passage of progressively darkening urine one day after running the marathon. gpt5_rationale: Post-marathon myalgias with dark urine and a urine dipstick positive for blood but no clear evidence of urinary tract pathology suggests pigmenturia from heme. Among the listed options, intravascular haemolysis best explains exercise-induced heme-positive urine.

stem: 64.9. A 52-year-old patient presents to your office with a left 4 cm histologically proven left breast carcinoma. On examination, she has a hard discrete mobile left axillary lymph node. gpt5_rationale: A 4 cm breast tumor is T2, and biopsy-proven ipsilateral supraclavicular nodal involvement is N3c, with no distant metastasis being M0. The correct TNM would be T2N3M0, which is not listed among the options.

stem: A 69-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department after a syncopal attack while shopping at the market. She has recently completed a two-week course of amoxicillin, omeprazole and clarithromycin for eradication of Helicobacter pylori. His wife also mentioned he has had diarrhoea for the past few days. Blood pressure is 90/66 mmHg and heart rate is regular at 98 bpm. Electrocardiogram done showed a prolonged corrected QT interval of 540 ms. While being monitored, a short run of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is seen on the cardiac monitor. What is the best intervention for this patient’s arrhythmia?
gpt5_rationale: This is torsades de pointes: polymorphic VT in the setting of marked QT prolongation, likely precipitated by clarithromycin and electrolyte loss from diarrhoea. The acute treatment of choice is intravenous magnesium sulphate, even if the serum magnesium is normal.

An 70 kg 28-year-old body builder reported to the ER with a 3-day history of intermittent colicky abdominal pain, total constipation, abdominal distension and 5 episodes of bilious vomiting. An NG passed yielded about a litre of bilious gastric fluid. Patient is being kept NPO as part of treatment, what is most appropriate fluid to use in the resuscitation of this patient.
gpt5_rationale: This is intestinal obstruction with significant extracellular fluid and chloride loss from vomiting/NG drainage, plus dehydration. Initial resuscitation is best with isotonic normal saline to restore intravascular volume and correct hypochloremic depletion.

stem: A 68-year-old man is admitted to an acute psychiatric unit for severe suicidal ideation. He is very much preoccupied with death and refuses to agree to a contract for safety. option_A: Persuade the patient to take antidepressants

option_C: Restrain the patient and administer intravenous fluids
gpt5_rationale: This patient has severe major depression with high suicide risk, refusal of food/fluids, and refusal of medications, making urgent definitive treatment necessary. Electroconvulsive therapy is indicated because it works rapidly and is especially appropriate in life-threatening depression when oral treatment is not feasible.

stem: A 60-year-old male with significant history of smoking presents with a 4 month history of epigastric pain with associated jaundice, weight loss and loss of appetite. His abdomen is soft but there is epigastric tenderness. An abdominal ultrasound showed a mass in the head of the pancreas. Which tumor marker is most likely to be elevated?
gpt5_rationale: This presentation is classic for pancreatic adenocarcinoma of the head of pancreas. The most associated marker is CA 19-9, but since it is not listed, CEA is the best available option.

stem: A 52-year-old man is hospitalized after a severe myocardial infarction. On the second day in hospital when his physician comes by on rounds the patient insists on jumping out of bed and doing several pushups to show the physician that ‘they can’t keep a good man down-there is nothing wrong with me!’ Which defense mechanism BEST DESCRIBES this patient’s symptoms?
gpt5_rationale: He is refusing to acknowledge the seriousness of his recent myocardial infarction and behaves as if nothing is wrong. This is classic denial.

stem: You are the house officer on duty when a patient reports with complaint of hearing voices commenting on his every action even though he doesn’t see anyone talking. You rightly determine that this person is experiencing
gpt5_rationale: Voices commenting on a person’s actions are classically third-person auditory hallucinations running commentary. 'Second person auditory hallucinations' are voices speaking directly to the patient as 'you,' so none of the listed options is correct.

stem: A 29-year-old woman attends A&E with a tender, swollen left breast. Her temperature is 38°C. She is two weeks post-partum and is breastfeeding. Ultrasound shows a cystic mass in the left breast. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
gpt5_rationale: This postpartum breastfeeding woman with fever, tender swollen breast, and a cystic mass on ultrasound most likely has a lactational breast abscess. The next step is needle aspiration of the collection, usually with antibiotics, while breastfeeding is generally continued.

stem: A 4 weeks old baby boy presents with a history of abdominal swelling and difficulty in passing urine. On evaluation and radiological examination, the baby is found to have posterior urethral valves. The parents seek to know the available treatment options from the doctor. All of the following are true except:
option_A: Emergency draining of the urine with a stent
option_B: Abrasion of the posterior urethral valves when the baby is stable
option_C: Vesicostomy is indicated when the baby is stable
option_D: Continuous monitoring of renal function is necessary
gpt5_rationale: Initial management of posterior urethral valves includes urgent bladder drainage, followed by valve ablation when stabilized, with ongoing renal function monitoring. Vesicostomy is generally reserved for cases where catheter drainage or primary ablation is not feasible, not simply because the baby is stable.

stem: A 67-year-old woman with a 25-year smoking history presents to the clinic expressing concerns regarding an increase in the size of her right breast over the last 4 months. On examination, you find a non-tender, mobile, lobulated 10 cm mass with relatively smooth edges in the right breast. The right breast is significantly larger than the left and has a 'teardrop' appearance. The most likely diagnosis here is:
gpt5_rationale: A large, soft, mobile, non-tender, lobulated breast mass with smooth edges and unilateral breast enlargement causing a teardrop appearance is most consistent with a lipoma. Abscess and inflammatory carcinoma are usually painful/inflamed, and fibroadenoma is more typical in younger women and usually smaller.

A 20-year-old woman is seen in clinic because of a thyroid nodule. She is asymptomatic and her past medical history is unremarkable. She takes no medications. There is a 1-cm fi rm, solitary, nodule in
the lateral aspect of the left lobe of the thyroid. A radionuclide scan showed no uptake of tracer in the nodule. Ultrasonography shows a solid, homogenous 1-cm mass. Fine-needle aspiration cytology
shows a follicular neoplasm. What is the next best step in management?
option_C: Incisional biopsy and enucleation if benign
gpt5_rationale: Follicular neoplasm on FNA cannot distinguish adenoma from carcinoma; the next step is diagnostic surgical lobectomy/hemithyroidectomy. None of the listed options matches that standard management.

stem: A 36 year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding at 8 weeks 3 days’ gestation. She has never been pregnant before. The bright red ’spotting’ started 3 days ago with no abdominal pain. Vaginal examination revealed a closed cervix. Which of the following is helpful in the diagnosis of this condition?
gpt5_rationale: This presentation is most consistent with threatened miscarriage, defined by vaginal bleeding with a closed cervix in early pregnancy. Transvaginal ultrasound is the key investigation to assess fetal viability and confirm the diagnosis.

stem: One day after unprotected casual sex encounter with a man recently diagnosed as HIV infected, a young lady undergoes an antibody-based HIV test that returns negative. What is the earliest time to reschedule a repeat HIV antibody test;
gpt5_rationale: An antibody-only HIV test is usually not reliably positive until about 3–12 weeks after exposure. The earliest practical repeat point among the options is 6 weeks, though later follow-up may still be needed depending on the test used.

stem: A 6-day old infant delivered at 31 weeks who has been hospitalized from birth develops recurrent generalized seizures without fever. Lumbar puncture yields a uniformly bloody cerebrospinal fluid. The most likely aetiological factor is:
gpt5_rationale: A preterm infant with recurrent afebrile seizures and uniformly bloody CSF most strongly suggests intracranial hemorrhage. Among the options, subarachnoid hemorrhage best matches this presentation.

stem: A 50-year-old man who was diagnosed of hypertension and started on Lisinopril 10 mg daily is referred to the Renal clinic due to hyperkalaemia and marked elevation in serum creatinine seen on on repeat kidney function test done after 2 weeks. What is the most useful investigation to identify the possible reason for this observation?
gpt5_rationale: A marked creatinine rise and hyperkalaemia soon after starting an ACE inhibitor strongly suggests renovascular disease, especially bilateral renal artery stenosis. CT renal angiography is the most useful test among the options to identify this cause.

stem: 11. A 45-year-old man who works on a cattle farm sustained an open injury of the foot after stepping on a nail that pierced through the boot. He was nursing the wound at home with an antiseptic solution. 2 weeks later she started having trouble moving his jaw. His back and neck became stiff and painful. He had worsening dysphagia and hesitancy on urination. He was rushed to the emergency of a local hospital after experiencing a seizure. What is the most like diagnosis of this patient
gpt5_rationale: The presentation is classic for tetanus: puncture wound, trismus, neck/back stiffness, dysphagia, autonomic dysfunction, and spasms/seizure-like episodes. Tetanus is not among the listed options, so none of the choices is correct.

stem: A 30 year old female presents with weakness of the lower limbs. On examination there is loss of proprioception and vibration sense. Here full blood count reveals increased mean corpuscular volume (MCV). What is the likely diagnosis?
option_C: Subacute combined degeneration of the cord
gpt5_rationale: Loss of proprioception and vibration with lower limb weakness suggests posterior column and corticospinal tract involvement. The raised MCV points to vitamin B12 deficiency, which classically causes subacute combined degeneration of the cord.

A 22-year-old patient with known rheumatic disease of the mitral
valve presents to thehospital with acute-onset pain in her right lower extremity. The limb is cool, and she describes a sensation of numbness and tingling. You are unable to appreciate pulses in the limb. Which of the following is TRUE of her management?

stem: A middle age man presents with acute onset ascending paralysis. He recounts that he had suffered a preceding diarrhoeal illness which he recovered from. Examination reveals flaccid weakness of both lower limbs. Which organism is most likely associated with this presentation?
gpt5_rationale: Acute ascending flaccid paralysis after a recent diarrhoeal illness is classic for Guillain-Barré syndrome. Campylobacter jejuni is the organism most commonly associated with this condition.

stem: A 60 year old woman presents with slurred speech and weakness involving the left side of the body. There is facial drooping to the opposite side of the body. On examination, tone on the affected side is increased with brisk reflexes. What is the likely arterial territory for this presentation?
gpt5_rationale: Left-sided increased tone, brisk reflexes, and weakness indicate an upper motor neuron lesion in the right hemisphere. Facial weakness and dysarthria with contralateral hemiparesis are most consistent with a right middle cerebral artery stroke.

stem: Lupus pernio is the term for chronic sarcoidosis-related indurated, lumpy, violaceous, blue-purple lesions. It can be disfiguring by eroding into underlying cartilage & bone. The lesions are classically located on?
gpt5_rationale: Lupus pernio classically affects the face, especially the nose and cheeks, producing violaceous indurated plaques. It is a chronic cutaneous manifestation of sarcoidosis.

stem: A 30-year-old male complains of leg weakness and paresthesias of the arm and leg. Five years previously he had an episode of transient visual loss. On physical exam, there is hyperreflexia, bilateral Babinski signs, and cerebellar dysmetria with poor finger-to-nose movement. When the patient is asked to look to the right, the left eye does not move normally past the midline. Nystagmus is noted in the abducting eye. A more detailed history suggests the patient has had several episodes of gait difficulty that have resolved spontaneously. He appears to be stable between these episodes. He has no systemic symptoms of fever or weight loss. Which of the following is the most appropriate next test to order?
gpt5_rationale: This presentation is classic for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, including internuclear ophthalmoplegia and prior optic neuritis. MRI of the brain and spinal cord is the most appropriate next test because it is the primary diagnostic study to demonstrate demyelinating lesions disseminated in space and time.

stem: A lady who is 4 months pregnant presents with some pain in her right knee with a swelling that has been increasing slowly in the previous 2 months. There is only a slight decrease in flexion but not much added pain. A radiolucent lesion is noted in the subchondral region of the distal femur.
option_A: It is important to counsel the lady about the possible amputation of the affected femur
option_B: Nothing should be done until the lady delivers her baby
option_C: Urgent surgery of the lesion should be considered
option_D: The patient must be prepared for chemotherapy once her baby is delivered
gpt5_rationale: A subchondral radiolucent lesion in the distal femur with mild pain and swelling in a pregnant woman is most consistent with a giant cell tumor, which can enlarge during pregnancy. These lesions require prompt orthopedic oncologic evaluation and generally surgical management rather than waiting until delivery.

stem: Iron released from enterocytes basolateral membrane binds to free sites on the plasma iron transport protein transferrin. Normal transferrin saturation is ~30%. Systemic regulation of iron absorption is mediated by?
gpt5_rationale: Systemic regulation of iron absorption is controlled by hepcidin acting on ferroportin, the basolateral iron exporter on enterocytes. DMT1 mediates apical uptake, ferritin stores iron, and serum iron is not the regulatory mediator.

A woman had an emergency caesarean section for a pathological CTG and pyrexiain labour She was discharged on postoperative day 4 but re-admitted on day 
6 with pyrexia, tachypnoea, tachycardia and hypotension. Haemoglobin is 105 g/l. Septic shock is the main differential diagnosis. Following the Sepsis 6 bundle, along with antibiotics and blood cultures, which other important blood test needs to be taken?
gpt5_rationale: The Sepsis 6 bundle specifically includes measuring serum lactate to assess tissue hypoperfusion and severity of sepsis. CRP, fibrinogen, and U&E may be useful, but lactate is the key test within the bundle.

stem: Two hundred children with severe ITP were enrolled in a randomized clinical trial to compare the rate of nose bleeds between children who received anti D therapy and those who receive no treatment. One hundred were assigned to each group. Which of the following is the most appropriate statistical procedure?
gpt5_rationale: The outcome is the rate/proportion of nose bleeds, a categorical variable, compared between two independent groups. A chi-square test is the appropriate procedure for comparing proportions between independent samples.

               decreased libido and absence of menses for 2 years duration. Her FSH

gpt5_rationale: A 50-year-old with 2 years of amenorrhea, hot flushes, night sweats, decreased libido, and elevated FSH is most consistent with menopause. The elevated FSH supports ovarian failure rather than pregnancy or hyperprolactinaemia.

stem: A 60-year-old male presents with complaints of dysphagia and a 6-kg weightloss. He states that four weeks ago, he noticed a 2 cm hard mass in the upperneck (Level II on your exam). You see an ulcerated mass in the left pyriform sinus on indirect laryngoscopy. The best next step to confirm the diagnosis should be:
option_A: An open biopsy of the neck mass
